Transcript:
[00:00] Jamal Rivera: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, this is Jamal on AE side, sophie and arjun from our SE and optimize teams. how are you all?
[00:08] Claire Thompson: doing well, thanks. excited to see the quantization stuff - we've got pretty heavy embedding and chat traffic so cost is creeping up.
[00:14] Rajiv Menon: yea, and latency matters for our live features. we hit p95 spikes that break our UX sometimes.
[00:19] Sophie Chen: cool, yep we'll focus on quality vs latency. today's walkthrough will cover INT8 and FP8 profiles, what quality delta you might expect, and how Optimize helps you pick the right profile per route.
[00:30] Arjun Patel: i'll start with the bench numbers we ran on a 7B decoder model - approximate numbers so they're directional. FP16 baseline p95 was ~160ms per request at our test batch. INT8 profile got p95 down to ~110ms, FP8 landed around 95ms in some kernels.
[00:48] Claire Thompson: wait - fp8 is faster than int8 in your tests? i thought int8 quant is usually smaller and faster?
[00:54] Arjun Patel: yeah common expectation - what happened here is the fp8 path we used leverages specialized tensor kernels and keeps some matrix ops in fp8 which reduces dequant/requant overhead; int8 required extra per-token conversions in our runtime for that model shape. results depend a lot on model architecture and sequence length distribution.
[01:12] Sophie Chen: + to add, int8 often gives slightly better deterministic compression for weights but fp8's dynamic range sometimes preserves rare-token behavior better, so you see smaller quality regressions for certain generation tasks.
[01:26] Claire Thompson: that matches some of our internal findings, rare-entity hallucinations spiked with a naive int8 run we did.
[01:32] Jamal Rivera: right, and that's why Optimize includes per-prompt evals and a quality monitor so you can see regressions per prompt set. we clobber down the metrics to BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies and also human-review flags.
[01:45] Rajiv Menon: curious about the measurement setup - what prompts and length distributions did you use? our traffic is short chatty requests, avg 40 tokens.
[01:53] Arjun Patel: we split tests across 3 buckets: chatty (avg 30-60 tokens), long-form (avg 250 tokens), and embeddings. the biggest performance delta shows up for long-form where kv cache behaviors and kernel selection matter. for short chat, both int8 and fp8 are solid and you typically get 25-40% latency reduction.
[02:13] Sophie Chen: worth calling out the quality drop numbers - for the LLM we used, INT8 gave a median quality delta ~3-5% on our automated metrics, FP8 ~1-2%. but again, some prompts had larger regressions - those are the edge cases Optimize flags.
[02:29] Claire Thompson: 3-5% could be too much for us on intent classification; we need <1% model drift. so we'd probably target fp8 if that buys us lower latency with acceptable drift.
[02:38] Jamal Rivera: absolutely - the Optimize flow can run per-route profiles so you can route sensitive routes to FP16 or FP8 and lower-risk routes to INT8. that hybrid approach usually gives the biggest cost win with minimal quality impact.
[02:52] Rajiv Menon: what's the rollback story if production shows more degradation?
[02:56] Arjun Patel: you get automatic rollback policies - we can set thresholds on your quality metrics or error budgets; if the metric crosses the threshold, traffic reverts to the pinned model/profile. all of this is surfaced in the Console with trace links to examples.
[03:12] Sophie Chen: also there are canaries and % rollouts in the Console - you can do 5% for 6 hours then 25%, we keep rollback quick.
[03:19] Sara Li (CTO): how invasive is this for our infra? we are leaning Hosted right now but may want Dedicated soon.
[03:26] Jamal Rivera: for Hosted API you just select the profile and Optimize runs the bench on our infra. for Dedicated we can run the same profiling harness against your Dedicated pool; the only requirement is access to the sample traffic and the ability to spin the same model variants. for Private (VPC), we provide the runbook and scripts to run locally with the same eval tooling.
[03:45] Claire Thompson: there was a mention of KV cache earlier - will quantization hurt cache hit behavior?
[03:50] Arjun Patel: good question. quantization doesn't change the logic of KV caching, but in some model implementations quantizing certain caches (or storing them in lower precision) can change numerical drift on long sequences. we recommend keeping KV cache in fp16 for long-dialog sessions and quantize the weight matrices that dominate compute. Optimize's profiles include those presets.
[04:11] Rajiv Menon: ok that helps. can you share the benchmark spreadsheet and scripts?
[04:14] Jamal Rivera: yeah - we'll share the spreadsheet and the exact scripts, plus a short README on how we measured p50/p95/p99 and quality proxies. link in the follow-up - e.g., slides: https://redwood.ai/deck/quant-profiles (note: internal link).
[04:28] Claire Thompson: perfect. about cost - ballpark savings moving from fp16 to fp8 or int8?
[04:33] Arjun Patel: savings depend on utilization, but typical unit-cost improvements are 25-50% for INT8 and 30-60% for FP8, because the latter can enable better kernel throughput on some hardware. again, your workload mix affects numbers.
[04:48] Sophie Chen: and Optimize gives per-route cost estimates based on your traffic - it will show monthly cost delta for trying a profile for a given route.
[04:56] Sara Li (CTO): we need guaranteed latency SLOs - can Redwood commit to p95 numbers?
[05:01] Jamal Rivera: for Hosted we publish performance profiles but SLA-based p95 guarantees come with Dedicated reserved capacity. we can size a Dedicated pool to meet your p95 targets and include that in a reserved capacity offer.
[05:13] Rajiv Menon: if we do a pilot on Dedicated, how long to get results?
[05:17] Arjun Patel: usually 1-2 weeks - we run benching, then real-traffic canary. for a 2-week PoC we can collect enough signal for quality and latency to recommend a rollout.
[05:26] Claire Thompson: ok that's our preference. one more question - what about quantization tooling for custom models? we run some fine-tuned variants.
[05:34] Sophie Chen: Optimize supports custom model onboarding - we have a quantization pipeline and can run profiling on your fine-tuned weights. there are extra steps for tokenizers/prompt templates but we do that as part of the onboarding.
[05:46] Jamal Rivera: noted - Claire you'll share sample prompts and a representative fine-tuned model snapshot if possible.
[05:51] Claire Thompson: can do, i'll sanitize and send.
[05:53] Jamal Rivera: great. any other open concerns?
[05:56] Sara Li: security/compliance - we'll need SOC2 docs and KMS/HSM integration info for Dedicated.
[06:03] Jamal Rivera: yes - we'll attach SOC2, ISO summary, and our KMS integration notes. for Private we can do HSM via our on-prem runbook.
[06:12] Rajiv Menon: would be good to see a cost estimate that includes Dedicated commit vs hosted with Optimize savings.
[06:18] Arjun Patel: i'll put together a side-by-side cost delta with assumed traffic and the expected per-token savings for FP8/INT8 and include infra commit pricing.
[06:27] Jamal Rivera: okay quick recap before we close - next steps: i'll share the benchmark spreadsheet, slides, and scripts by Friday (2026-07-09). Claire to share prompt sets and SLOs by 2026-07-10. Arjun to prepare Dedicated pilot estimate and runbook by 2026-07-12. we'll plan to kick PoC week of 2026-07-13 and do a 2-week test.
[06:48] Claire Thompson: that sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:50] Sophie Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links.
[06:55] Jamal Rivera: thanks, meeting over.
